Hello everyone,
I am looking for a theorem stating conditions for the unit of a left Kan extension in a double category (or in a 2-category) to be an isomorphism, some sort of generalisation of the pointwise+fully faithful condition (see e.g. corollary 6.3.9 in Category Theory in Context of Emily Riehl). Do you know if such a thing exists?
I've looked at Grandis&Paré's On weak double categories, parts III and IV and Koudenburg's On pointwise Kan extensions in double categories where they discuss pointwise extensions but I have not found anything about the unit being an isomorphism.
Thanks!

What definition of left Kan extension are you using, or what is the setting in which you wish to apply such a theorem? For instance, if you are working in the setting of an equipment, this is proven in Lemma 3.29 here.

I am working in a 2-category of virtual double categories (with some properties, namely cartesian virtual equipments) and am wondering about the extension of some virtual double functor.
I asked about extensions in double categories because I felt like most work is done in that setting and is only more "expressive" than in 2-categories (?)
Anyway, the result you mentioned should be enough for me. Thank you for pointing that out, I'll have a read

To talk of left extensions of virtual double categories, you really need to work in a virtual double category: VDCs do not form a double category, merely a VDC. 2-categories are also insufficient, as the representably fully faithful 1-cells in the 2-category of VDCs are not the fully faithful functors of VDCs (see §2.4 here). So, the result I linked to should indeed be the most appropriate for your purposes.
